definitions.explanation: An exam given to students who missed the original exam or failed to pass, often due to illness or other valid reasons.

examples.japanese: {風邪|かぜ}で{試験|しけん}を{休|やす}んだので、{追試|ついし}になった。
examples.english: I missed the exam due to a cold, so I have to take a make-up exam.

examples.japanese: {追試|ついし}は{本試験|ほんしけん}より{難|むずか}しいという{噂|うわさ}がある。
examples.english: There's a rumor that make-up exams are harder than the regular exam.

notes:
{追試|ついし} is an abbreviation of {追試験|ついしけん}. It refers specifically to an exam given to students who missed the original exam for valid reasons such as illness or emergencies.

KEY DISTINCTION:
- {追試|ついし}: make-up exam (for those who missed it with valid reason)
- {再試験|さいしけん}: retake exam (for those who failed and need another chance)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {追試|ついし}を{受|う}ける: to take a make-up exam
- {追試|ついし}になる: to end up having to take a make-up exam
- {追試|ついし}の{届|とど}け{出|で}: a make-up exam request form

RELATED EXAM VOCABULARY:
- {本試験|ほんしけん}: main/regular exam
- {期末試験|きまつしけん}: final exam
- {中間試験|ちゅうかんしけん}: midterm exam
- {追試験|ついしけん}: make-up exam (full form)
